reason: The cited evidence supports that low-temperature annealing introduces L12 precipitates in the fcc phase (E2, E3) and that coherent L12 nanoprecipitates strengthen alloys (E1, E2). However, no evidence is provided for the key premises that the untreated alloy's brittleness is specifically due to dislocation pile-ups at interfaces, that precipitates can be selectively localized at inter-lamellar boundaries, or that such interfacial precipitates would mitigate pile-ups and enhance ductility. These mechanistic claims are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: L12 nanoprecipitates can be introduced in the fcc phase of Al0.7CoCrFeNi by low-temperature annealing
Coherent L12 nanoprecipitates strengthen the alloy via Orowan mechanism
The untreated eutectic HEA has limited ductility due to dislocation pile-ups at lamellar interfaces
Precipitates can be selectively localized at inter-lamellar interfaces by controlled aging
Interfacial precipitates will mitigate dislocation pile-ups and improve ductility while retaining strength
